suggested_issue_title: Aspose.Page FOSS for Python: published package metadata names no project URL
suggested_issue_body:
## Summary

At revision `43cef367cd0b2cf00cc03064ca9d29d1ff507967`, the package metadata declares no project URL. The `aspose-page-foss` 26.9.0 release on PyPI therefore has no `home_page` and no `project_urls`: its page links to neither the source repository nor the issue tracker.

## Environment

- Repository: aspose-page-foss/Aspose.Page-FOSS-for-Python
- Revision: `43cef367cd0b2cf00cc03064ca9d29d1ff507967` (the upstream revision this report was verified against, default branch `main`)
- Verified on 2026-10-11 from a fresh shallow clone; the PyPI read is the public JSON API.

## Steps to reproduce

```
grep -n -i 'url' pyproject.toml setup.py
grep -c '^\[project.urls\]' pyproject.toml
curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/aspose-page-foss/json | python -c 'import json,sys; i=json.load(sys.stdin)["info"]; print(i["home_page"], i["project_urls"])'
```

## Expected

The package metadata names the repository, `https://github.com/aspose-page-foss/Aspose.Page-FOSS-for-Python`, as a project URL, so the PyPI page links to the source.

## Actual

- The first command prints nothing: neither `pyproject.toml` nor `setup.py` mentions a URL.
- The second command prints `0`: there is no `[project.urls]` table.
- The third command prints `None None`: PyPI lists no `home_page` and no `project_urls` for 26.9.0.

## Suggested fix

Add a `[project.urls]` table to `pyproject.toml` with `Repository = "https://github.com/aspose-page-foss/Aspose.Page-FOSS-for-Python"` (and `Issues`), make sure `setup.py` forwards it to `setuptools`, and publish a release, since PyPI shows the metadata of the release only.
